name: Résidence Étudiante Jouvence
sub: When subtle shades reveal the true depth of the architecture.
builder: NOVAOM – The City and Metropolis of Dijon
story: The Jouvence student accommodation, designed by A2A Architectes, features a contemporary and understated architectural style in the heart of a dynamically developing neighbourhood. The various building blocks are united into a single entity by a subtle gradation of mineral shades on the concrete façades. This gives the complex a distinctive yet understated identity and allows it to blend harmoniously into its urban surroundings. KEIM Concretal-Lasur was used for the project.

name: University College London
sub: Protecting concrete in the long term
story: University College London (UCL) is situated in Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park and comprises several buildings, including Marshgate – a 35,000 m² academic centre for creativity and interdisciplinary research, which forms the centrepiece of UCL East. A KEIM water repellent was selected by the London-based architectural firm Stanton Williams to be applied to the internal concrete surfaces, where it serves as a dust barrier. A series of units spans eight storeys, each featuring collaborative spaces for exhibitions and internal conferences.

name: Franklin Village
sub: Colour makes all the difference
story: With the award-winning “Franklin Village” development in Mannheim, sauerbruch hutton demonstrates how sustainable timber construction, social quality and strong design can work in harmony. The colourful design of the pergolas, achieved using KEIM Lignosil-Color, plays a key role in this. The result is a durable colour scheme that lends the housing project its identity and atmosphere.

name: Cyber City
sub: Innovation meets architecture
story: Tesonet has opened the new “Cyber City” in the Naujamiestis district of Vilnius – an innovative centre on the site of the former Sparta sock factory. The site is home to Tesonet’s headquarters and its portfolio companies, as well as amenities such as restaurants and bars, a gym, co-working spaces, conference rooms, green recreational areas and an innovation lab. The black finish of the surface was achieved using KEIM Concretal.

name: Schule Brno
sub: A school steeped in history
products: KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Silangrund, KEIM Contact Plus
story: The technical school on Sokolská Street was founded in 1885. It was the first Czech technical school in Moravia and Silesia. The building that stands there today is already the third school building and the second to have been built specifically for the school. The initial design was drawn up by the architects Vilém Berger and Karel Welzl (both of whom were teaching at the school at the time) in collaboration with the headmaster, Vojtěch Dvořák. The new building was completed remarkably quickly: construction began on 1 May 1900 and was finished in July 1901 – that is, after just 14 months.

name: Concert Hall of National Musical School
sub: Excellent architecture for music
story: Where music meets the city, architecture with character emerges: the new concert hall at the State Music School in Jastrzębie-Zdrój sets new standards not only in terms of acoustics but also in terms of urban planning, demonstrating how an educational building can become a vibrant public space. The architectural concept of the project is based on the balanced interplay between the concert hall, foyer and public space in the existing urban environment. The aim was to create a building that blends naturally into the urban space while also reorganising it.

name: Conservatory Varieté
sub: A theatre that enchants even from the outside
products: KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Design-Lasur, KEIM Restauro-Lasur, KEIM NHL-Kalkputz-Grob, KEIM NHL-Kalkputz-Fein
architect: MASKE + SUHREN Architekten und Designer Gesellschaft von Architekten mbG
story: The traditional Wintergarten Varieté Berlin, long known for spectacular productions and big names in show business history, is now also making an impressive architectural statement: extraordinary linear LED lighting bathes the striking façade of the 19th-century building in atmospheric light in the evening hours – warm, inviting and a real eye-catcher. Lighting solution from Barthelme LED Solutions, specialising in customised linear LED lighting solutions for architecture, design and industry.

name: Museum of Decorative Arts
sub: Historic architecture with a modern design concept
story: The Neo-Renaissance building of the Brno Museum of Applied Arts was built in the 19th century and is now home to the Moravian Gallery in Brno and the new ART DESIGN FASHION concept. The main aim of the interior renovation was to integrate the idea of presenting contemporary designers through their designs for interior elements and spaces. KEIM Soldalit and KEIM Restauro-Lasur were used for this purpose.

name: Haus Moench
sub: Keeping the spirit alive
products: KEIM Armierungsmasse-100, KEIM Brillantputz, KEIM Lignosil-Verano, KEIM Lignosil-Color, KEIM Marano-Roll
architect: AMU Architekten Dipl. Ing. Univ. Architekt Andreas Müller
story: In the midst of the rolling hills of Chiemgau, on the edge of a forest, stands a carefully renovated farmstead with historical roots dating back to the 15th century. Just a few metres away, a small new building complements the ensemble. The architect and builder has not only renovated and rebuilt here, but has also sensitively created a connection between centuries-old building fabric and contemporary, sustainable living. The aim was to preserve the soul of the property while creating modern living space. The farm has a long history.

name: Community Foundation Wangen am Klösterle
sub: Nordic spruce in elegant blue
story: The aim of the Wangen Community Foundation is to show solidarity and use its assets where they bring lasting benefits. The new Am Klösterle residential complex is a particularly successful example of this. The timber-framed building stands on a plot of land purchased by the city near the old town. The apartments are each just under 50 square metres in size. The ground floor has been designed as an inviting communal area, which is available for health promotion activities such as gymnastics, dance or yoga and offers opportunities for socialising. Germany has a shortage of around half a million homes.

name: Floating House
sub: Ageing in harmony with nature
story: Design by Studio F. A. Porsche – under this label, Carinthian timber construction specialist GRIFFNER presents its new two-storey luxury prefabricated house made of wood and glass. The first show house in the series, called Floating House, was built at the company's headquarters in Griffen – a sustainable, two-storey timber construction with rooms up to 5.85 metres high, enveloped by continuous facade bands.

name: Grimming Bridge
sub: A bridge made of concrete and steel
story: The Grimming Bridge is a road bridge over the Trautenfels roundabout at the Trautenfels transport hub in Pürgg-Trautenfels. In spring 2021, the Grimming Bridge at the intersection between the Enns Valley and the Ausseerland region was opened to traffic. This marks the end of decades of wrangling over a solution for the critical traffic junction on the Ennstal Road (B 320). At 135 metres long, the Grimming Bridge is the longest integral bridge in Austria. More than 3,400 cubic metres of concrete and 650 tonnes of steel were used in its construction. A KEIM-Concretal glaze was applied.

name: Carl Wooden Hybrid High-rise Building
sub: Sustainable construction meets architecture
architect: Peter W. Schmidt + Assoziierte GmbH & Co. KG
story: CARL in Pforzheim is currently the tallest timber hybrid high-rise building in southern Germany. The 14-storey building represents a successful combination of sustainable construction, well-thought-out design and clear architecture. The project also uses wood as a durable, natural material for the facade design. KEIM Lignosil-Verano, a silicate greying glaze that gives the wood an even, pre-greyed appearance at the factory, was used. It provides the wood cladding with lasting protection against the effects of weathering and prevents irregular discolouration due to varying weather conditions.

name: Municipal Office Zell am Pettenfirst
sub: Warm grey meets oak wood
architect: Schneider Lengauer Pühringer Architekten ZT GmbH
builder: Johann Stockinger | Timber construction: TRAGWERK+ Ingenieurholzbau
story: The Zell am Pettenfirst community centre, designed by architects Schneider Lengauer Pühringer from Neumarkt im Mühlkreis, was coated with KEIM Lignosil-Verano silicate grey glaze. The warm grey tone continues harmoniously on the interior walls and ceilings. Oak floors, panelling and window frames provide a striking colour accent. The building was awarded the Upper Austrian Timber Construction Prize 2025 for its special architecture. Incidentally, the church in the background was also recently professionally renovated with KEIM plasters, KEIM Granital and KEIM Romanit.

name: Christ Church Luenen
sub: Impressive colour scheme
story: The christ church in Luenen, built in 1913/14 by Reinhold Becker, impressively demonstrates how art and architecture can enter into a harmonious dialogue with its new colour scheme. The interior was redesigned by artist Ulrich Reimkasten with horizontal lines of colour in soft pastel shades. With the aid of a laser project, the lines were precisely marked throughout the room and then traced. Reimkasten, whose work often combines traditional elements with contemporary accents, deliberately uses colours that reflect the incident light in a special way.

name: Residential Complex in Ulm-safranberg
sub: Sustainable living, stylish living
story: A residential project that sets new standards has been created on the Safranberg in Ulm. Built in modern timber hybrid construction, seven architecturally impressive houses combine elegance, style and an unrivalled living experience. The harmonious combination of warm wooden elements and stable concrete not only creates an aesthetic ambience, but also forms the basis for climate-friendly, ecological and future-proof living. This diverse neighbourhood is more than just a place to live - it is a living space that combines comfort, sustainability and individuality.

name: Farmhouse in Bavaria
sub: Stories on the facade
story: Lüftlmalerei is a traditional art form that has adorned facades in the Alpine region for centuries. Its roots go back to the 18th century, when ornately painted facades became a trademark of Bavarian and Tyrolean villages. The detailed motifs tell stories from the lives of the inhabitants, religious scenes or historical events. While this traditional art form has been increasingly forgotten in modern construction, it is experiencing a renaissance thanks to Bernhard Rieger, as the Wallgau artist reinterprets Lüftlmalerei and gives it a modern dimension as "Alpine street art".

name: Palazzo Turati
sub: Timeless elegance in Milan
story: The historic Palazzo Turati in the heart of Milan is a masterpiece of Italian architecture. The palace was built in 1880 by architect Henry Combi and has a rectangular floor area of around 60x40 metres around a central open courtyard surrounded by arcades with cross vaults. Its elegant façade and classical design make it a true symbol of Milan's cultural and architectural heritage. It has been the seat of the Milan Chamber of Commerce since 1954 and is also used as an event centre. Executing painting company: Impresa dei Restauro Gasparoli Srl

name: Czech National Museum Prague
sub: General refurbishment of a historic building
products: KEIM Soldalit-Arte, KEIM Innotop, KEIM Reversil, KEIM Reverfix, KEIM Lotexan
colours: KEIM Exclusiv 5196 and 9008, KEIM Edition Historical 50017
story: The National Museum in Prague is one of the most important Czech museum institutions and buildings in Prague. Built between 1885 and 1891, the neo-Renaissance building underwent a complete renovation. For more than two years, KEIM's technical experts applied a wide range of samples to reference surfaces, coordinated colours, opacity and appearance, tested processes and compositions, and also checked the winter resistance of the materials, among other things. The historic facade of the National Museum has been restored to its former glory and now once again adorns Prague's Wenceslas Square.

name: The Palace Madrid Hotel
sub: New splendour for historic jewel in the heart of Madrid
story: One of Madrid’s most iconic buildings shines again! The 8,000 m² facade of the historic Hotel Palace (1912) has been faithfully restored using KEIM mineral paints. The restoration process integrated sophisticated scientific techniques alongside the expertise of restoration specialists and craftspeople from various trades. Multiple layers of previous paintwork had to be removed, with sampling and laboratory analyses conducted to determine historically accurate colours for their subsequent restoration.

name: Weleda Cradle Campus
sub: Award-winning architecture for certified natural cosmetics
story: The new Cradle Campus in the Ostalb district is just as sustainable as Weleda's cosmetic products. In addition to a modern administration and functional building, it also includes an innovative high-bay warehouse. It is considered the most sustainable logistics center in Europe and can accommodate over 17,000 pallets. The project used traditional construction techniques and materials that are particularly sustainable and climate-friendly: rammed earth, clay plaster, and wood. The decision to use wood as a building material alone saved 2,600 tons of CO2.

name: Schwyz Town Hall
sub: Historic 1891 Mural Art on Schwyz Town Hall
story: In 1891, Ferdinand Wagner painted the Schwyz Town Hall with scenes from Swiss history — part of the 600th anniversary of the Swiss Confederation. Created using Keim’s mineral paints, the murals are considered technically and artistically outstanding. Their vivid colours were officially praised in 1913. In 1989/90, a careful restoration focused on stabilising the render to preserve the artwork. In 1890, the National Council and Council of States decided to celebrate the 600th anniversary of the Swiss Confederation in Central Switzerland.

name: Leibniz Institute for Astrophysics
sub: Built with the forest in mind
architect: Thomas Müller Ivan Reimann Gesellschaft von Architekten mbH
story: The extension to the Leibniz Institute for Astrophysics is situated in the middle of a wooded park landscape. The architects at Thomas Müller Ivan Reimann used the topography of the hillside property to embed the building in the forest instead of displacing it. In the interests of sustainability and to create a connection with nature, the new building's facade was given a wooden facade that was coated with the silicate-based greying stain KEIM Lignosil-Verano. Wood was also used for the interior fittings and furnishings of the institute.

name: Grand Hotel Łódź
sub: Historical charm becomes a five-star experience
products: KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Restauro-Lasur, KEIM Turado, KEIM NHL-Kalkputz-Fein, KEIM Dolomitspachtel, KEIM Innostar
story: The Grand Hotel in Łódź, a vibrant university and industrial city in Poland, has been the epitome of prestige and elegance for 135 years. Following a comprehensive renovation in 2023, it now harmoniously combines historical splendour with state-of-the-art five-star comfort. With 152 luxurious rooms and flats, two exquisite restaurants, an elegant café and unique conference rooms, including an impressive historic theatre hall, the hotel meets the highest standards.

name: Kraków Cloth Hall
sub: Historic trading centre and jewel of the Renaissance revived
products: KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Granital, KEIM Restauro-Lasur, KEIM Universalputz, KEIM Universalputz-fein, KEIM Biosil
story: The Cloth Halls are located in the centre of Krakow's main market square. It owes its name to the cloth trade, one of the most important goods sold here. It is considered one of the most important examples of Renaissance architecture in Central Europe. Today it houses a branch of the Krakow Historical Museum with an impressive collection of Polish paintings and sculptures from the 19th century. There are also numerous souvenir shops and craft stalls on the ground floor. The entire building was extensively renovated from 2009-2010. Numerous KEIM products were used for the design of the facade and interior.

name: Barrier-free Residential Building - Berlin Prinzregentenstrasse
sub: Inclusive living in the heart of Berlin
products: KEIM Klassik-Plus-MW, KEIM Stucasol, KEIM Innostar, KEIM Innotop, KEIM Concretal-Lasur
story: A special residential building has been created in a backyard in the heart of Berlin: barrier-free and inclusive. People with disabilities, students and families with children in need of care live here under one roof. Sustainability was also at the forefront of the new build and the building was constructed using a timber frame construction and a mineral insulation system from KEIMFARBEN.

name: Cadfem Headquarters
sub: Perfect mix: timber frame meets reinforced concrete
story: For its new office building in Grafing, CADFEM chose the right material in the right place: wood as a load-bearing element, as a façade and as interior cladding. Reinforced concrete for the basement, emergency staircases and technical rooms. The star-shaped building is intended to reflect the company's philosophy and, in addition to ecological concerns, to enable contemporary working in the sense of 'New Work'. Munich-based architects nbundm, who were responsible for planning and implementing the project, fulfilled this wish.

name: Rezidenca Kaimi Apartments
sub: Modern residential architecture with vibrant colour schemes and a high quality of life in Tirana
story: In collaboration with BLOX Architecture, the modern residential project KAIMI was built in Tirana, near the Ali Demi district and in the immediate neighbourhood of Mangalem 21. The residential complex comprises six buildings with numerous small and large apartments tailored to the needs of families of different sizes. The colourful facade design in blue, red, yellow, green and orange gives the quarter a modern and appealing look. A special design element is the repetition of the facade colours in the window embrasures, creating a harmonious overall appearance.

name: Partisan Hill
sub: Historical jewel revives - a piece of Wroclaw's history in new splendour
products: KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Turado, KEIM Porosan-Trass-Sanierputz-NP, KEIM Porosan-Trass-Zementputz, KEIM Porosan-Ausgleichsputz-NP
story: Partisan Hill (Bastion Sakwowy) was once an important part of Wroclaw's 16th century defences. It protected the city until 1807, before Jérôme-Napoléon Bonaparte conquered Wroclaw and the fortifications were demolished. This paved the way for the green city promenade, which was created according to the plans of Johann Friedrich Knorr. A hill with old casemates remained as a silent witness to the past. After an extensive two-year restoration by Castellum sp z o.o., the building now shines in new splendour and is once again open to the residents of Wroclaw.

name: House in the Park
sub: Facility for assisted living in Berlin-Pankow
story: The ‘House in the park’ is based on a community-orientated approach to create affordable living space in an ecological and sustainable timber hybrid construction. The new building is supplied with electricity and hot water via photovoltaics and heat pumps in conjunction with geothermal probes, which enables economic efficiency without fossil fuels. The new SkF residential project for people with physical and cognitive disabilities is being built in Berlin-Pankow, surrounded by a large park and three heritage-listed buildings.

name: Centennial Hall Wroclaw
sub: A masterpiece of modern architecture and engineering
story: The Centennial Hall in Wroclaw, Poland, is located in the eastern part of the city, surrounded by Szczytnicki Park. Built in 1913 by Max Berg, it is considered a masterpiece of modern architecture and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2006. With a free span of 65 metres in diameter, the dome was the largest of its kind in the world at the time of completion. The hall can fit over 10,000 people and is used for cultural, sporting and business events. Its innovative construction and monumental size make it an architectural landmark.

name: Jung Founder's Villa
sub: Historic JUNG founder's villa turns into a modern think tank
colours: vert anglais pâle (32042), vert anglais clair (320412), blanc ivoire (4320B), gris clair (32013)
story: The former residence of company founder Albrecht Jung in Schalksmühle has been given a new function as a think tank and meeting and service centre for the JUNG brand. The historic villa from 1928 was renovated and extended with a modern pavilion by the architects NGA Nehse & Gerstein BDA from Hanover as part of an open architectural competition. However, the building does not play the role of a showroom, but serves as a multifunctional office, event and residential building. During the refurbishment and operation, the values of responsibility, attitude and efficiency took centre stage.

name: Suburb House
sub: Redesign of a 1950s house for contemporary family life
architect: ORA - originální regionální architektura s. r. o.
story: The project involves adapting a semi-detached house from the 1950s to the needs of a large family. As modern family life no longer takes place strictly in individual rooms, a large shared living space was to be created. To this end, the ground floor was opened up and the attic utilised. The combination of living and play areas creates a feeling of togetherness. On the outside, the house opens up towards the garden with a glass veranda, but remains largely unchanged towards the street in order to preserve its original character.

name: BART 19th Street Station Oakland
sub: Oakland underground station upgraded
colours: Innostar Monochrom 9001S und 9006S, Design-Lasur Metallic 2/3 1002 und 1/3 1001
story: The 19th Street underground station is located in the middle of Uptown Oakland, near the historic Paramount Theatre on Broadway. MG Engineering has modernised Oakland's underground station to optimise mobility, the environment and traffic. Elements such as the new station cabin, the glass art railing and the five foot high glass barriers improve accessibility and visibility and reduce fare evasion. A new lift and bicycle racks increase passenger capacity. The energy-saving LED lighting increases safety and the fresh, light-coloured surfaces make it easier for passengers to find their way around.

name: Weisbach House
sub: From ruin to piece of jewellery
story: The Weisbach House in Plauen, one of the last surviving Baroque manufactory buildings in Saxony, was a ruin after the Second World War. After initial repairs in the 1990s, the city of Plauen decided to completely renovate the building in 2015 so that the ‘Factory of Threads’, a museum that brings together the collections from the Plauen Lace Museum and the Vogtland Museum, could move in. After restoring the outer structure of the building, the late baroque plaster façade with its yellow-ochre colour scheme was reconstructed. This also included painting the façade with KEIM Soldalit façade paint.

name: Hotel pod Roza
sub: Historical jewel from the 14th century with modern restoration
products: KEIM Granital, KEIM Granital-Grob, KEIM Ecosil-ME, KEIM Restauro-Lasur, KEIM Restauro-Fuge
story: The Hotel Pod Różą in Krakow, the oldest in the city, dates back to the 14th century and is located in a Renaissance palace. The architecture combines Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque elements. The interiors offer historical charm with vaulted ceilings and antique furniture. Modern renovations preserve the historical character. The facade and the entire interior of the hotel were restored between 2001 and 2003 and have been continuously renovated since then. Among other things, the hotel owners opted for KEIM Granital and KEIM Granital-Grob, which was also used in the interiors due to its "classic character".

name: Kuwait International Airport
sub: Modern terminal sets new environmental standards and optimises passenger comfort
story: Kuwait International Airport is being expanded into an air hub. In 2022, a modern terminal by Foster + Partners was added, offering a high level of comfort and new environmental standards. It is designed to be climate-friendly, inspired by local shapes and materials. The central building with a height of 25 metres and three symmetrical wings forms a giant cloverleaf. The roof protects against heat, lets in daylight and uses photovoltaic panels to generate energy. This creates a pleasant indoor climate despite the extreme outside temperatures.

name: Xeptum Consulting AG - Headquarter Place X
sub: Innovative "place X" headquarters: Xeptum combines nature and industry with a timber façade
story: With the new "place X" headquarters of Xeptum Consulting AG in Neckarsulm, Anna Philipp and her team of architects have created an innovative working environment that combines cosiness and efficiency. The IT company's office building harmoniously combines the industrial and natural environment: four wings extend from a central foyer into the vineyards. Green roofs, a wooden façade and photovoltaic systems emphasise the company's ecological and sustainable approach.

name: Amstel Station Amsterdam
sub: Impressive Peter Alma mural in the Amstel railway station
products: KEIM Innostar, KEIM Royalan, KEIM Soldalit
colours: KEIM Royalan 9058,  KEIM Innostar 9058, 9325, RAL 7038, RAL 7023, RAL 9010
story: The Dutch painter Peter Alma was best known for his impressive murals in Amsterdam's Amstel railway station in 1939. As a pioneer of "De Stijl", an abstract art movement, he devoted himself primarily to murals in transport buildings. His winning design 'The global significance of the railway system and its technical progress' impressed the Amstel Station jury with its composition, colour palette and simplicity. The execution was challenging, as the surfaces were 20 metres wide and 9 metres high.

name: Stuttgart 21
sub: Shades of Grey - Concrete design at Stuttgart 21 railway station
products: KEIM Concretal-Base, KEIM Concretal-Fixativ, KEIM Concretal-Lasur
story: The new concourse at Stuttgart's main railway station is a masterpiece of engineering. Designed by ingenhoven associates and Frei Otto, the freely curved shell roof is nearing completion: the concrete surfaces were carefully reworked to emphasise the elegance of the flowing forms. The company beconart used KEIM products for this purpose. Stuttgart's future main station forms the centrepiece of the major Stuttgart 21 project. An underground, 8-track through station will replace the existing 16-track terminus station.

name: New Construction in Kirchenfeldmatt (muri)
sub: The harmony of serially designed buildings
products: KEIM Brillantputz, KEIM EPS- Dämmplatten, KEIM AquaROYAL-Color
story: In Kirchenfeldmatt in the Swiss municipality of Muri, 104 owner-occupied and 42 rental flats have been built. Dachtler Partner Architekten created sixteen simple structures that offer maximum open and green space despite the loss of nature. Together with Jörg Niederberger, the facades were designed with vertical grooved plaster, using alternating, complementary shades of biocide-free mineral paint. Niederberger focused on the design potential of plaster structures and colours, with the colour mood varying depending on the viewing angle and distance.

name: Building Ensemble Glint Berlin
sub: Historic ensemble of buildings in Berlin-Mitte revitalised
story: On Glinkastrasse in Berlin-Mitte, a multi-part ensemble of listed buildings has been extensively renovated. All four of the GLINT's Wilhelminian-style buildings date from 1873 to 1886 and are typical examples of their time. The buildings were severely damaged during the Second World War and only poorly renovated during the GDR era. The renowned architectural firm von Bothmer has succeeded in transforming the historic into the modern, preserving the neoclassical character of the buildings and giving room to new impulses.

name: Stadtcasino Basel
sub: Sophisticated timber construction in neo-baroque language
story: The Stadtcasino has been a gem in Basel since 1876 and, together with the nearby theatre, the Historical Museum and the Kunsthalle, forms a cultural hotspot in the city. The renovated and extended music hall of the Stadtcasino Basel was reopened in summer 2020. The extension by Herzog & de Meuron is characterised by a special wooden facade that visually echoes the neo-baroque stone architecture of the building, which was built in 1876. To give the existing music hall more space for the required extension, various options and variants were analysed.

name: Einstein Tower
sub: In the name of science: restoration of the Einstein Tower in Potsdam
story: The Einstein Tower was planned on the initiative of Erwin Finlay Freundlich to prove Albert Einstein's theory of relativity. Erich Mendelsohn, an innovative architect, designed the observatory with an experimental approach, integrated the telescope into the architecture and made creative use of reinforced concrete. Despite pioneering ideas, this led to planning and structural problems that made it difficult to maintain. After almost 100 years and a refurbishment in 1997-1999, extensive damage required a new restoration, financed and carried out by the Wüstenrot Foundation.

name: Andreas Quartier Düsseldorf
sub: Conversion of the old courthouse in Düsseldorf
products: KEIM Reversil, KEIM Optil, KEIM Soliprim, KEIM Concretal-W, KEIM Soldalit
architect: slapa oberholz pszczulny | sop GmbH & Co. KG | architekten
story: In the centre of Düsseldorf's old town, a new quarter has been created around the former district and regional court: the Andreas Quartier. It was built on an 18,000 square metre site and comprises flats, offices, restaurants and a hotel. The starting point for the Andreas Quartier is the neo-baroque listed former court building with a large columned portico at the main entrance. Behind the historic building, which is part of the neighbourhood, the newly built residential and living quarter is grouped around two inner courtyards.

name: Sprzeczna 4
sub: Award-winning apartment building in modern prefabricated construction
story: The residential building at 4 Sprzeczna Street in the Praga-Północ district of Warsaw was built entirely from prefabricated construction elements and was completed in just four months. Modern materials and technologies were used for the design. Sprzeczna 4 has received several awards, including the Warsaw Mayor's Architecture Prize in the category ‘Best Building’ and first prize in the 21st ‘Polski Cement w Architekturze’ competition. The building was put As some prefabricated elements required colour correction, KEIM Concretal-Lasur was used for colour matching.

name: Municipal Apartments in Córdoba
sub: Municipal housing project in Spain with 104 social housing units
story: In Córdoba, Andalusia, architect César del Pino of UNIA Arquitectos has designed an urban housing project with 104 social housing units. The facades are made of prefabricated concrete slabs and are an example of the increasing innovation in the industrialisation of the building sector. For the coating of the exposed concrete, a colour was sought that would help to reduce the maintenance costs of the buildings, and the choice finally fell on the particularly durable product KEIM Soldalit. The colour design was another important challenge.

name: Yas Marina Circuit
sub: A masterpiece of racetrack architecture
story: The Yas Marina Circuit is a 5.554-kilometer-long racetrack in Abu Dhabi, designed by the German racetrack designer and civil engineer Hermann Tilke. One of the most prominent features of the Yas Marina Circuit is its location on Yas Island, an artificial island extending off the coast of Abu Dhabi. The track is renowned not only for its technical challenge and demanding curves but also for its unique architecture. The entire racetrack and surrounding facilities are architecturally designed to meet the highest standards for motorsport events.

name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
sub: Architectural jewel in the heart of Milan
products: KEIM Granital, KEIM Contact Plus, KEIM Dekorfarben
story: The Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II is located in the heart of Milan, between Piazza del Duomo and Piazza della Scala. Opened in 1867, it is one of the oldest shopping centres in the world. The impressive neo-Renaissance architecture is characterised by a glass dome and a magnificent steel frame that spans the elegant shopping arcades. Mosaics and elaborate decorations adorn the floor, while the cross vaulting creates a harmonious combination of classicism and modernity. The Galleria is a popular meeting place and a landmark of Milan.

name: Hotel Mandarin Oriental Ritz
sub: The hotel the king wanted.
architect: Luis de Landecho und Lorenzo Gallego
story: The Hotel Ritz in Madrid, a splendid 5-star luxury hotel, was inaugurated in 1910 by King Alfonso XIII and is currently operated by the Mandarin Oriental Hotel Group. It was commissioned at the request of King Alfonso XIII, who, upon returning from a European tour, realized that Spain lacked a suitable hotel to host European kings and other prominent guests. The magnificent building was designed in 1908 by the renowned French architect Charles Frédéric Mewes and was constructed between 1908 and 1910 under the supervision of architects Luis de Landecho and Lorenzo Gallego.

name: Educational Centre Ban Cologne
sub: Networked education: The innovative education project of Cologne
story: "Bildungslandschaft Köln" is a pilot project realised as an educational alliance comprising eight educational and recreational institutions under municipal and independent sponsorship in the Cologne district of Altstadt-Nord. To this day, it remains a municipal research initiative, having set new standards in educational construction during both the planning phase and the construction process. The ambitious architectural endeavor was conceived by the architectural firm gernot schulz: architektur in Cologne and spanned a period of 13 years from inception to completion.

name: Day Care Centre Waldstetten
sub: Kindergarten "Berg-Wichtel" is wholesome and convenient
colours: 32090 rouge vermillon, 4320W le jaune wif, 32052 vert clair
architect: Klaiber + Oettle Architekten und Ingenieure GbR
story: The kindergarten by Klaiber + Oettle in Waldstetten was described by a councilwoman as "square, practical, good!" It integrates well into the existing school and hall system, providing short distances, clear structures, and transparency. The concept supports children and educators, enabling swift planning and operational flexibility. Significant emphasis was placed on healthy construction using verified, low-emission building materials, overseen by the Sentinel Hause Institute. The pollutant measurement confirms the success.

name: Zayed International Airport
sub: Innovative airport design: Zayed International Airport combines culture with functionality
story: The terminal at Zayed International Airport in the United Arab Emirates impresses with a roof construction of wide-span arches and a towering, wave-shaped roof inspired by sand dunes and geometric patterns. To keep out the desert sun, the roof has been drawn over the facade, requiring less glazing and no external shading. Head of Design at KPF Mustafa Chehabeddine emphasises that the design references the cultural and natural environment of Abu Dhabi.

name: Residential Complex Krummer Weg
sub: Sustainable timber construction creates affordable housing
story: STADTBAU GmbH Pforzheim has realised a residential development on Krummen Weg in Pforzheim that for the first time in the Northern Black Forest region includes subsidised flats in pure timber construction. This demonstrates the compatibility of affordable, socially balanced housing and climate protection. The flats are characterised by bright, friendly rooms with a wood scent, floor-to-ceiling windows, open kitchens and underfloor heating. Sheltered loggias facing south offer additional comfort. The construction project comprises 49 flats of different sizes in three wooden buildings.

name: Parliament Building
sub: New parliamentary committee building: modern architecture harmoniously complements the historic Sejm complex
story: The building of the parliamentary committees is located near the Sejm at 1 Wiejska Street. It was designed in 2001 by the architectural firm Stelmach i Partnerzy, which won the competition for the Sejm complex. With a total area of 10,000 m², of which 8,000 m² is above ground, part of the building extends under the street and the Old House of Deputies and is connected to the Sejm complex on the other side of the street. The light-coloured concrete facade blends harmoniously into the surroundings and was designed in consultation with the monument protection authorities.

name: Light Tower Solingen
sub: An extraordinary place in the Bergisches Land
story: The Lichtturm is a former water tower in Solingen-Gräfrath, located on the edge of a nature reserve. The tower's former water reservoir is now a light-flooded glass-domed hall with a great view of the Bergisches Land and an ideal venue for conferences, workshops or cultural events. The lower floors serve as an extraordinary showroom for the regionally and sustainably produced light collection of the company Licht im Raum. After 15 years, the tower received a new coat of KEIM Twinstar in the upper area. The painting was carried out with the help of a variable working platform.

name: Plaza Mayor Y Casa de la Panadería
sub: A great example of the durability of KEIM paints
story: The history of the most popular square in Madrid dates back to the 16th century. In 1590, construction began on the Casa de la Panadería, which was the first building in the new square. Its facade was decorated with frescoes from the beginning. During the last major restoration of the building in the early 1990s, the damaged plaster was renewed and the facade was decorated with the current mural of mythological figures by Madrid artist Carlos Franco, using KEIM decorative paints.

name: Housing Estate Klushof
sub: How unrenovated post-war buildings in Bremerhaven were revived and are now making a name for themselves.
products: KEIM AquaRoyal-System, KEIM Stucasol, KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Klassik-System
story: In recent years, the housing company STÄWOG in Bremerhaven has modernised two neighbourhoods of plain residential buildings from the 1950s and made some of them barrier-free. In doing so, it has taken unusual paths - in order to preserve affordable housing and to promote cooperation among tenants. The project by architect Hans-Joachim Ewert was completed back in 2018 and was awarded the Bremen Housing Prize 2025 last year. It had also received the national award ‘Gegen den Strom – Soziale Stadt Wulsdorf’ as early as 2019.

name: Hotel Riu Plaza España
sub: A colossus in the centre of Madrid
story: In 1948, construction began on what was then the tallest building in the city of Madrid, at 117 metres. With its central location, the building is an icon of the city, and the spectacular view from the roof provides a view of a large part of the capital. Throughout its history it has been used as a hotel, although some of the 26 floors are used as office space. After two years of complete interior renovation, it opened in 2019 as the Hotel Riu Plaza España.

name: Siegfriedviertel District of Braunschweig
sub: A listed building is being insulated
products: KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Klassik-MW, KEIM Pulverkleber, KEIM Brillantputz
story: The energy-efficient modernisation of a listed facade using historical plastering techniques is a demanding task that requires preserving the beauty of the facade while combining it with the useful. The gatehouse of the listed building complex in Braunschweig's Nordstadt district, which spans several streets, was to be fitted with an ETIC system as a pilot project. The plaster facades from the 1930s were finished with a special comb-pull technique, which had to be reproduced on the surface of the thermal insulation. At the beginning of planning, surface techniques on ETIC systems were still little known.

name: Wroclaw Railway Station
sub: Historical heritage restored with a modern approach
products: KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Optil, KEIM Biosil, KEIM Restauro-System, KEIM Silex-OH, KEIM Lotexan-N, KEIM Reversil, KEIM Concretal-Lasur
story: The complete refurbishment of Wroclaw Central Station from March 2010 to June 2012 was a major project that included the restoration and redesign of the entire building ensemble as well as the renewal of the technical infrastructure. A particular focus was on the restoration of valuable artefacts such as decorative paintings, ceiling paintings and historical furnishings. All work was subject to strict conservation requirements. One of the challenges was to convert or adapt numerous interior rooms and room complexes to new forms of use by carrying out some major remodelling work.

name: Casa de América
sub: Historic Foreign Affairs Building
story: The Palace of Linares is currently home to LA CASA DE AMERICA, a cultural institution founded in the 1990s and sponsored by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Municipality of Madrid and the Madrid City Council, which is used for conferences and exhibitions of the countries of the Americas in Madrid.

name: Cine Callao
sub: Probably the most famous cinema in Madrid
products: KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Contact Plus, KEIM Universalputz-fein
story: In the Plaza de Callao, the cinema of the same name has been located since 1926, the first work of the architect Luis Gutiérrez Soto and probably the most famous cinema in the Spanish capital. The building in Art Deco style is one of the landmarks of the city centre. Different sections of the façade are divided by squares covered with a continuous sgraffito of stylised vases and rays, similar to the brocade patterns made in interiors by the great French designer Jacques Émile Ruhlmann.

name: Círculo de Bellas Artes
sub: The Círculo de Bellas Artes is a private, non-profit, cultural organisation.
story: The Círculo de Bellas Artes is a private, non-profit cultural institution. The headquarters of the Círculo de Bellas Artes, designed by the architect Antonio Palacios and located on Calle Alcalá in Madrid, was built in the early 1920s and inaugurated by King Alfonso XIII in 1926. It is one of the most important private cultural centres in Europe, with an extensive cultural programme that includes performances and exhibitions ranging from the visual arts to literature, science, music, philosophy, film and the performing arts.

name: Residential Complex Becrux
sub: Avant-garde architecture in Madrid
story: An avant-garde residential complex has been built on one of Madrid's busiest streets. Its curved lines of fibreglass-reinforced concrete create a friendly and unique facade that, together with the volume of the adjacent tower, forms a complex visible from afar just a stone's throw from the centre of the capital.

name: Walt Disney World Swan Reserve
sub: A facade that shimmers like a lake
story: The Swan Hotel, also known as the Walt Disney World Swan Hotel, is a luxury resort located within the Walt Disney World resort complex in Florida, United States. It was operated by the hotel chain Westin Hotels & Resorts, which is part of Marriott International. Designed by world-renowned architects GENSLER, the hotel's all-glass facade and colour scheme offers a contemporary interpretation of the Florida resort while paying homage to the Swan & Dolphin, originally designed by Michael Graves. KEIM Soldalit was used for the coloured design of the facade.

name: Hotel Four Seasons
sub: Spectacular refurbishment project in the heart of Madrid
story: In the heart of Madrid's historic centre and close to the Parliament is a block of seven historic, monumental buildings that were home to banks in their heyday but had been unused for years. In an intervention lasting several years, the team of architects in charge of the project managed to unite these individual buildings and transform them into a complex for hotel use, luxury flats and commercial space.

name: Hotel Drumlerhof
sub: Nature and sustainability in the Dolomites
story: In the idyllic village of Sand in Taufers, in the midst of the impressive Dolomite landscape of South Tyrol, rises the climate-neutral Hotel Drumlerhof. The hotel concept focuses on respectful interaction with nature and people. The Innerhofer-Fauster family, who run the hotel, attach great importance to local producers and use only fair trade products. Their long-standing public good balance measures and evaluates their sustainability efforts. The Drumlerhof is passionate about protecting the earth for future generations.

name: Battersea Power Station
sub: Battersea Power Station in London: Transformation into a modern residential and commercial zone
story: The former Battersea Power Station in London was converted into a shopping mall with offices and flats by Wilkinson Eyre on behalf of a Malaysian investor. The original appearance of the turbine halls was largely preserved. The power station, built between 1929 and 1955, supplied one fifth of London's electricity needs. The central boiler house is flanked by two symmetrical turbine halls, followed by the electrical control centres. The complex's four chimneys, more than 100 metres high, make it a well-known landmark of London's industrial age.

name: Mangalem 21
sub: In Albania's capital Tirana, the largest and most colourful housing project to date was built
products: KEIM Stucasol, KEIM Brillantputz, KEIM Design-Lasur-Gold
story: On the outskirts of Tirana, the architectural firm OMA has built the largest residential project since the end of communism. In order to structure the ensemble of around 1200 flats in a varied way, the architects relied on a sophisticated colour concept - and on the proven luminosity and colour stability of KEIM. Learn more about Albania's largest housing project - realised by the Office for Metropolitan Architecture (OMA).

name: Westhouse Augsburg
sub: "To offer people a place to meet, to be inspired, to be engaged, as well as to reflect on what is essential in life." That is the idea of the Westhouse.
products: KEIM Lignosil-Color, KEIM Lignosil-Verano, KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Coolit
story: In Bavaria, a multifunctional centre has been created that combines work, leisure and meeting under one roof. From the outside, a noble silver-grey wooden facade is impressive, which also helps the building to blend in perfectly with its surroundings. "To offer people a place of encounter, inspiration, engagement as well as reflection on the essentials in life." - That is the idea behind the Westhouse on the outskirts of Augsburg. Especially today, in a fast-paced, digital age and after various pandemic-related lockdowns, places of encounter are becoming more important again.

name: Marina Bay Sands
sub: Luxury resort and landmark of Singapore
story: Marina Bay Sands is a luxury integrated resort in Singapore that opened in 2010. The 20-hectare resort was designed by Moshe Safdie Architects, who used stacks of playing cards as a template. Located on the shores of Marina Bay, it comprises an impressive ensemble of three 55-storey hotel towers, a huge conference and exhibition centre, a shopping mall, an art and science museum, two theatres, numerous restaurants and bars, an infinity pool and a rooftop garden. The resort is a Singapore landmark and attracts millions of visitors from all over the world every year.

name: Fort Van Den Bosch
sub: Historic fortress in Indonesia shines in new splendour
products: KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Innotop, KEIM Porosan-Trass-Sanierputz-NP
story: Benteng Pendem, also known as Fort van den Bosch, is a fortress in Pelem, Ngawi, Indonesia. In the 19th century, Ngawi was an important trading and shipping centre in East Java. The fort was completed by the Dutch in 1845. During World War II, it was used as a prison by the Japanese. It was then abandoned and gradually deteriorated into a ruin surrounded by nature. In February 2019, it was announced that it would be rebuilt, and in the years that followed, the fort was reconstructed through extensive restoration work. Today, it shines again in new splendour and is sure to attract many tourists.

name: Lazienki Palace
sub: The "Palace on the Island" - significant cultural heritage in the Royal Basque Country Warsaw
story: The history of the Łazienki Palace, also called "Palace on the Water" or "Palace on the Island", dates back to the second half of the 17th century. The palace passed through the hands of many important owners up to Tsar Alexander I. Between 2012 and 2014, the team of Restauro Sp. z o.o. from Toruń carried out difficult restoration work on the facade of the palace, using KEIM Romanit lime paints and KEIM Restauro glaze. Today, the Palace on the Waterfront is under the care of an independent institution, the Royal Łazienki Museum in Warsaw.

name: Ilot Saint-urbain
sub: Colours that create a sense of togetherness
story: The mineral stain KEIM Concretal plays a decisive role in the redesign of the Ilot Saint-Urbain residential and commercial block in the heart of Strasbourg. The multifunctional residential complex of 21,542 m² consists of eight buildings, each clad in different shades of colour. The colours serve as a unifying element between the different buildings and create a visual contrast with the surrounding landscape. The colour selection was developed by the two architectural firms LAN and TOA especially for this project.

name: Hochhaus Langen Feldbergstrasse
sub: Sustainable facade art for a residential tower
products: KEIM Klassik-MW, KEIM Brillantputz, KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Coolit, KEIM Design-Lasur
story: "Size matters" - while a huge banner with this provocative lettering on the facade of the 18-storey high-rise in Feldbergstraße in Langen was still attracting attention, work began behind it on a spectacular facade design. In just seven weeks, grey concrete gave way to an abstract-naturalistic painting with a blue sky, white clouds, deceptively real trees and an illusionistic zoo. The artist Ulrich Allgaier, who specialises in exclusive murals, was responsible for this.

name: Santa Maria Goretti Church
sub: In Mormanno, Italy, a modern parish centre with a green heart was built.
story: In the heart of the Pollino National Park lies the small mountain town of Mormanno, among whose hills the Church of Santa Maria Goretti has recently been built. With its organic architecture, the concrete building constructed by MC A - Mario Cucinella Architects, winner of the CEI 2011 pilot project, sets new standards. Not only is it based on the shape of a four-leaf clover, it also provides healthy air itself. For this purpose, it works with an air purification process inspired by nature: a facade coating with KEIM Soldalit-ME breaks down nitrogen oxides via photocatalysis.

name: Stieglerhof
sub: Building, living and working in harmony with nature
story: A major fire destroyed all the historic buildings of the three-sided farm in 2014. With architect Peter Dürschinger, the farm ensemble was recreated. Local sandstone stands as a reminder of the history of the Stiegler farm and was complemented with traditional timber construction from the farm's own spruce and pine. The use of these two building materials for construction and facade shapes the buildings of the Hazelnuss-Hof into a haptic unity.

name: Holzmann Waldshut
sub: New life has been breathed into a villa from the 1930s.
products: KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Innostar, KEIM Stucasol, KEIM Dolomitspachtel, KEIM Soliprim, KEIM Algicid-Plus, KEIM Porosan
architect: Klaus Keller. Andy Keller. Kathrin Keller. Architekten PartGmbB
story: In Waldshut-Tiengen, near the Swiss border, new life was breathed into a 1930s villa with old trees. The old villa from southwest Germany still contained some of the previous owners' interior furnishings from the 1930s and had to be structurally renovated to meet the needs of the new owners. The architects therefore created a home for a young, growing family with space for a modern, flexible lifestyle. The residential building from the 1930s, which was still partly equipped with the original fixtures from that time, was to be structurally renovated and adapted to the usage requirements of the new owners.

name: Munich Volkstheater
sub: A colourful spectacle not only on stage
products: KEIM Innenfarben, KEIM Innostar, KEIM Soliprim
builder: Landeshauptstadt München, Kommunalreferat vertreten durch das Baureferat
story: The stage is the heart of an event - the new Volkstheater the heart of the Schlachthofviertel in Munich. With the conversion and new construction of the Munich Volkstheater, the architects from LRO Lederer Ragnarsdóttir Oei created not only a combination of old with new, but also a balance of monochrome and colourful. Seen from the outside, the brick-red facade blends harmoniously into the surroundings of the old cattle yard area. The large archway creates an "arc of tension" from the listed part of the building to the new building, which allows visitors to experience the history of the site.

name: Headquarters Josef Rädlinger
sub: New company headquarters for the Josef Raedlinger Group of Companies
credit: Petra Kellner Amberg / Berschneider + Berschneider GmbH
story: New company headquarters for the internationally active Josef Raedlinger group near Cham in the Bavarian Forest. A new three-storey building in monolithic solid brick construction relates to the neighbouring former Windischbergerdorf monastery, which was renovated and converted in parallel. In order not to dominate the monastery building too much, the building was partially modelled into the sloping terrain .For the exterior and interior of the building solely ecological and durable materials were used.

name: Brenner Research House
sub: Stuttgart star architect Alexander Brenner has built his own house and used it for experimenting.
products: KEIM Design-Lasur, KEIM Dekorfarben, KEIM Athenit-fino
credit: Zooey Braun / Alexander Brenner Architects, Stuttgart
story: The Stuttgart architect Alexander Brenner has made a name for himself by designing residential buildings and villas for a demanding clientele. Now he has built his own house and used this opportunity for a few experiments. Behind 75-centimetre thick walls, there are surprisingly light, wide rooms. Various surfaces treated with KEIM products characterise the interior.

name: Marina One
sub: The "Green Heart" is considered an international role model for living and working in mega cities.
products: KEIM Concretal-Lasur, KEIM Concretal-Fixativ, KEIM Silan-100
story: Marina One in Singapore is a special building complex: four skyscrapers form the framework of a central three-dimensional garden - for a better interaction of working, housing and living. In particular, glass, steel and certified green concrete were used for the construction. Ensuring the longevity of the concrete in humid tropical climates is a challenge for major projects of this kind. The tropical city state of Singapore is situated on the southern tip of the Malay peninsula between Malaysia and Indonesia.

name: Galleri Lene Bilgrav
sub: Four artists' different approaches to painting
credit: Ensuite, Galleri Lene Bilgrav, 2022. Works by Peter Holm and Milena Bonifacini, colored walls by Bodil Nielsen. Photo: Jacob Friis-Holm Nielsen
story: The exhibition Ensuite is curated by Katrine Hvid and shows painting, sculpture and installation. The majority of the works are created for this exhibition and for a dialogue with each other. The four artists have in common that their work is based on painting, both as a medium and as a model. In this exhibition, they will show works that fluctuate between the two-dimensional and the threedimensional. The title of the exhibition Ensuite refers to the procedural course in the creation of the exhibition and points out that the collegial interaction is an essential curatorial grip for the exhibition.

name: Dengel House Reutte
sub: Women's power makes historic facade shine
products: KEIM Universalputz, KEIM Turado, KEIM Soldalit-Arte
builder: Tiroler Friedenswerk gemeinnützige Wohnbaugesellschaft m.b.H., Rum (AT)
credit: Hornstein & Co. KG Malerei & Vergoldung, Reutte (AT)
story: The Obermarkt 3 house is undoubtedly one of the most beautiful and powerful buildings in the market town of Reutte (Tyrol). In 2020, an elaborate restoration took place. Extraordinary design competence was expected in the process. The craftsmanship and design achievements of the past became the challenge of the present. The employees of Hornstein & Co. KG Malerei und Vergoldung took on the task with respect and gave the building new splendour. The contract for the restoration of the facade went to the company Hornstein & Co. KG Malerei & Vergoldung, a Reutter family business in its 4th generation.

name: Ines Innovation Center
sub: Office building for research and innovation of the Universidad del Bio-Bio in Concepción (Chile).
story: The two architects Mauricio Pezo and Sofia von Ellrichshausen created a new innovation centre on the Collao Campus of the University of Bío-Bío in Concepción (Chile). With the design, they wanted to show how a simple multi-storey building can become spatially complex. All six floors are slightly different as the proportions of the circles gradually change from floor to floor. "This is an apparently simple, stable and regular building that contains an unexpected and exaggerated interior," said Pezo and Von Ellrichshausen.

name: The Imprint
sub: The "gold piece" in Seoul's Paradise City has no windows, but an expressive facade.
story: Not far from South Korea's largest airport Incheon is "Paradise City", an amusement and entertainment centre that was expanded in 2018 with two illustrious new buildings. "The Imprint" houses a nightclub and the "Wonderbox", an indoor entertainment park. Because both uses do not require natural lighting, it was possible to do without windows and reduce the building volumes to plain cubes. But the architects from MVRDV transformed the cubic idea into a very unique staging through a sophisticated façade concept.

name: State Institute for Apiculture
sub: Those who build for nature inevitably build naturally.
story: If you build for nature, you inevitably build naturally. With this in mind, the State Institute for Apiculture was constructed as a sustainable building using a timber hybrid construction method. The façade is allowed to age by itself over the years. To ensure that it remains beautiful in the meantime, it was pre-greyed. Bees, honey and honeycombs: These topics are the focus of the State Institute of Apiculture, a unique institution of a university in Germany.

name: Zeitz MOCAA
sub: In Cape Town, a historic grain silo has been transformed into a museum of African art.
products: KEIM Concretal-Fixativ, KEIM Concretal-Feinspachtel, KEIM Concretal-Mörtel-R, KEIM Concretal-MKH, KEIM Betonschnellreiniger, KEIM Concretal-Lasur
story: In Cape Town, a historic grain silo has become a museum for contemporary African art. The architects of Heatherwick Studio had the concrete walls of the granaries sawn open, creating an atrium of almost cathedral-like character. New concrete reinforces the old silo walls - it was only after being treated with KEIM-Concretal that it met the planners' requirements. It is a real magnet for the public: In the first month after its opening, 70,000 people flocked to the Zeitz Museum of Contemporary African Art (MOCAA).

name: Castle Kummmerow
sub: After the sleeping beauty
story: After its slumber and extensive renovation measures, Kummerow Castle now houses a top-class photographic collection. Torsten's castle on Lake Kummerow impresses with an extraordinary renovation concept that preserves the traces of the past and visibly only adds new things where flaws have appeared. It has been open to the public since 2016 and houses Kunert's collection of international photography, which is well worth seeing. The current owner of the castle, Torsten Kunert, bought the castle at an auction.

name: My.o Munich
sub: The green colour dates back to an old Munich tradition.
builder: CA Immo München Nymphenburg GmbH & Co. KG
story: The green colour goes back to a Munich tradition - there are some very good examples of this from the 1920s in particular. In combination with the hand-applied plaster, the dull green blends well into the context. It draws attention, but is not obtrusive. The material world and generosity of the entrances and stairwells hark back to the qualities of historic office buildings.

name: Edificio Guridi Bilbao
sub: The Guridi building is one of the few examples of Spanish Art Nouveau (Modernismo) in the city of Bilbao.
story: The 6-storey Guridi building was designed in 1902 by the architect José Bilbao y Lopetegui and is located on Calle Licenciado Poza, in the heart of the Ensanche district. KEIM Soldalit was used to paint the exterior of the building during its most recent refurbishment, which was carried out in 2020/21. The unique colour scheme of the building required an absolutely colour-stable paint so that the facade would remain unchanged for many years.

name: Metro Madrid Headquarters
sub: In the north of Madrid, in the Tetuán district, the new headquarters of Metro Madrid is being built.
architect: Nexo Arquitectura & Gutiérrez - De La Fuente Arquitectos
story: In the north of Madrid, in the Tetuán district, the new headquarters of Metro Madrid is being built. This building complex consists of a total of six buildings. The first two buildings were completed in 2021. They form the heart of the new Metro Madrid headquarters and house the company's new administrative and technology centre on up to 12 storeys, with state-of-the-art workplaces for around 1,000 people. A second phase of the project will see the construction of the other buildings, which will house other functional areas of Metro Madrid as well as a museum dedicated to transport.

name: The Black House
sub: An almost sculptural character: the Bohl single family house
story: In the new development area of the small town of Wolfhagen in northern Hesse lies the black house built in timber frame construction by the architect couple Nina and Michael Bohl. The house is an eye-catcher - and not only because of the dark exterior facade. The architects had the idea of creating a dark, rough, but clearly contoured body. A body that on the one hand is eye-catching, but on the other hand can also take a back seat in the neighbourhood of white houses with dark gable roofs and windows.

name: Prinz-eugen-park
sub: Livable, lively and excellent: The ecological model settlement in Prinz-Eugen-Park Munich.
products: KEIM Lignosil-Verano, KEIM Lignosil-Inco, KEIM Biosil, KEIM Optil, KEIM Lignosil-Color, KEIM Concretal-Lasur
colours: Keim Lignosil Verano im Sonderfarbton MT 8013496 M
story: Housing is a basic need and affordable housing is an important element of social cohesion - but it is in short supply, especially in Germany's large cities and metropolitan regions. To address this problem, the city of Munich seized the opportunity in developing the site of the former Prinz Eugen barracks and set social and ecological standards through the allocation of the land. A quarter with 1,800 flats has been created that serves as a model for the whole of Munich and far beyond.

name: Livensa Living Studios
sub: In Bilbao, Spain, you will find Livensa Living Studios, a student residence with modern studio flats.
story: Near the Nervión River, in the northwest of Bilbao, you will find Livensa Living Studios, a student residence completed in 2021 with modern studio flats. In one wing of the building, studio flats can also be rented for short stays in Bilbao. Because of its proximity to the universities, but also because of its good location between the old town and the Bilbao Exhibition Center "BEC", the location of Livensa Living Studios is ideal for students, for city travellers and trade fair visitors. Colour played a central role in the design of the facade of this building complex.

name: Üstra Housing Estate
sub: In Hanover, the largest timber housing estate in Lower Saxony was built with 139 rental flats and a daycare centre for children.
story: On the site of the former ÜSTRA light rail depot in Hanover, a housing estate for the ÜSTRA's utility facility was built with 139 rental flats and a day care centre for children. The new wooden housing estate is considered the largest in Lower Saxony to date.

name: Practice Wiesendeck Vohenstrauss
sub: It does not get any greener than this: building and nature become one
story: The wave-shaped "Wiesendeck" building in Vohenstrauß (district of Neustadt/Upper Palatinate) is a real eye-catcher. Architect Volker Schwab and Alexander Riedl, Holzbau Riedl from Waldthurn-Lennesrieth, realised the project with a very high demand for sustainability. Together with the clients, the ecological idea was important to them from the very beginning. The wave-shaped "Wiesendeck" building in Vohenstrauß (district of Neustadt/Upper Palatinate) is a real eye-catcher.

name: Frauenfriedenskirche
sub: 'Frauenfrieden' Frankfurt: A place of worship filled with art and colour
story: One of Germany's most amazing sacred buildings stood in full colour when it was built in the 1920s. After extensive destruction during World War 2, the Frauenfriedenskirche was rebuilt, but remained unimpressive for decades with grey walls and barely recognisable paintings. From 2018 to 2020, the church was thoroughly renovated and restored. With the newly designed chancel, it now shines again in the colourfulness of its construction period. One of Germany's most amazing sacred buildings stood in full colour when it was built in the 1920s.

name: Silent Rock
sub: On a slight slope, with a charming view of the town centre of Bammental, a vacation home made of black exposed concrete was built.
story: Built in 2015, the two-story weekend house in Bammental appears as a dark monolith whose walls and roof were uniformly realized in lightweight concrete. Like an angular, hollowed-out stone, it blends unobtrusively into the surrounding landscape as a "silent rock" - no matter from which side you approach it - and creates a symbiosis of architecture and nature.

name: Concordia Design
sub: On Poland's Słodowa Island in Wrocław, a place was created that combines work and pleasure.
products: KEIM Soldalit-ME, KEIM Concretal-Lasur, KEIM Concretal-Black, KEIM Optil, KEIM Innostar
story: Concordia Design has created a building complex that brings together versatile uses in one place: Work and event spaces, a food hall, a café and a roof terrace with a view of Słodowa Island make the listed 19th century building an attractive destination for visitors.

name: Cultural and Congress Centre Jordanki
sub: The Jordanki Cultural and Congress Centre is located in Toruń, Poland and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
story: The Jordanki Cultural and Congress Centre lies like an embedded rock in Poland's medieval UNESCO World Heritage city of Toruń. Due to a particularly roughly worked concrete structure, the building complex looks like a cave both inside and out. The building was designed by the Spanish architect Fernando Menis. With its brick interior, it makes reference to the nearby old town of Toruń. The building has already received several awards. Among others, it was considered one of the 7 new Polish wonders by National Geographic.

name: Euregon Headquarter
sub: New company building for software developers in timber frame construction with a feel-good climate.
story: The state-of-the-art office building of the software development company euregon AG is located in the middle of the greenery of Augsburg's Sheridan Park. A friendly and inviting office landscape extends over three floors, which could be designed freely and flexibly thanks to the wooden skeleton construction in BauBuche.

name: Church St. Dionysius
sub: In the church of St. Dionysius, impressive paintings have brought us even closer to heaven.
story: Contemporary repainting or conservation of the existing building? This was the decision facing the congregation of the Roman Catholic parish church of St. Dionysius in Elsen, a district of Paderborn. As part of the extensive renovation of the listed church building, the decision was made in favour of an artistic re-painting by the internationally renowned artist Tobias Kammerer from Rottweil, thus bringing contemporary art into the church rooms.
