name: Gallery House at 5 Cardiff Grove
sub: The Gallery House in Singapore stands for human-centred design, enjoyment, innovation and sustainability.
architect: CIAP Architects Pte Ltd, MJKY Architects
credit: CIAP Architects Pte Ltd; MJKY Architects
story: To accommodate both living and work spaces for an architect and an artist, Gallery House at 5 Cardiff Groove was designed with a human-centric approach. The house also embodies design attributes aligned with the national sustainability agendas — such as incorporating passive cooling and water management, as well as buildability and wellness.

name: Eco Timber Housing Estate Meerleben
sub: Only 800 m from the Baltic Sea beach, people could put their alternative living ideas into practice.
story: A construction consortium is building a village of fully ecological timber frame houses on the Baltic Sea. The holistic design without pollutants sets an example for both raw materials and society as a whole. In order to realize their alternative ideas of building, living and housing, people of different ages and lifestyles have joined together to form a building community. For the 7,700 m² site near Wismar, which is located only 800 m from the Baltic Sea beach, the development plan envisaged a village-like vacation home settlement that can be used by the owners themselves as well as rented out.

name: Childcare Centre „sonnenschein“
sub: "I have a house, a colourful house...", warbled Astrid Lindgren's Pippi Longstocking.
story: The facades of kindergartens are usually eye-catchers: they often draw attention to themselves in a cheerful and colourful way - Sometimes the kindergarten facade already gives an indication of the concept of the institution from the outside. This is also the case with the Kindergarten "Sunshine" in southern Germany, whose facade is designed in different ways with wood. According to Managing Director Martina Knorr, the hobbyhorse of Eurokindergarten GmbH from Warthausen, which specialises in building kindergartens, is ecological and climate-neutral construction.

name: Kneipp Nursery School
sub: Natural facade seamlessly blends the nursery school into the landscape
story: The facades of nursery schools are usually eye-catchers: they are often cheerful and colourful - sometimes the facade of the nursery school gives an indication of the concept of the institution from the outside. This is the case with a Kneipp nursery school in southern Germany, whose facade has been designed in a variety of ways using wood. The single-storey structure of the Kneipp kindergarten in the Lower Bavarian town of Vilsbiburg, made of wood studs, is very economical due to its simple construction.

name: Childcare Centre „between Forest and Lake“
sub: Chestnut, lime, oak, maple - the strong reference to the forest also inspired the colour design.
story: Nursery school facades are usually eye-catchers: they often attract attention in a cheerful and colourful way - Sometimes the nursery school facade already gives an indication of the institution's concept from the outside. This is also the case with the Kindergarten "Between Forest and Lake" in southern Germany, whose facade is designed with wood in various ways. The name of the kindergarten "Between Forest and Lake" in Zusmarshausen already reveals a lot about the educational concept of the facility. The children are to be familiarised with nature and explore their environment in a variety of ways.

name: Hotel Warszawa
sub: Historic concrete foundations serve as a design element and add playful design accents.
products: KEIM Concretal-Lasur, KEIM Innotop, KEIM Intact, KEIM Restauro-Lasur
story: The Hotel Warszawa in Warsaw, Poland's capital, can be seen from over 20 kilometres away. Built between 1931 and 1933, at 66 metres high it was the tallest building in Poland and the second tallest in Europe. Originally built as the headquarters of the English insurance company Prudential, it was designed in the Art Deco style. Severely damaged after the war, it was rebuilt in the 1950s and served as a hotel until 2002. After being renovated by a hotelier family from Krakow, it was reopened at the end of 2018 as a luxurious five-star hotel with 142 rooms and various amenities.

name: Hotel Nobu
sub: What do Oscar winner Robert De Niro and Japanese celebrity chef Nobu Matsuhisa have in common?
products: KEIM Concretal-Lasur, KEIM Concretal-Fixativ, KEIM Lotexan
architect: Medusa Group, Przemo Lukasik und Lukasz Zagala, Warschau
story: What do the former second largest building in Europe and a hotel by Robert de Niro have in common? The design with concrete! On the facade of one building and in the interior of the other, this material plays a striking role. Exposed concrete once had a bad reputation, but today it is impossible to imagine the world without it. Its natural grey colour conveys a certain elegance and timelessness, but it can also be coloured. The Hotel Nobu in Warsaw presents itself in a completely different way: it combines a historical building with a newly built, modern wing.

name: Iser-quartier
sub: Even the welcome sign in the entrance area makes it clear: something special has been created here.
products: KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Concretal-Lasur, KEIM Innostar, KEIM Innotop
architect: Baulinie Architekten, Gläser & Lehmann, Architektenpartnerschaft mbb
story: A newly built cooperative residential quarter in the Allgäu region is making a name for itself: With its architecture, its special colour scheme and the smallest details, the extremely well thought-out settlement refers both to its bohemian past and to its surroundings. The final touch is given to the quarter with high-quality colour products. Even the welcome sign in the entrance area of the new Iser Quarter in Neugablonz, Bavaria, makes it clear: something special has been created here: Each of the houses bears the name of a personality who comes from the Reichenberg region in former northern Bohemia.

name: Beethoven House
sub: Just in time for Beethoven's 250th birthday, the most popular music museum gets a fresh new look
products: KEIM Universalputz-fein, KEIM Universalputz, KEIM Innostar
story: The Beethoven House in Bonn received a newly conceived exhibition in time for the 250th anniversary of the composer's birth, in which the building itself also takes on a more central role. Renewed mineral plasters and paints in the interior play their part and put the exhibits in the right light. About 100,000 tourists from all over the world gather every year in a small alley in the centre of Bonn not far from the Rhine. They marvel at a house with a rather inconspicuous facade and explore the rooms behind it, because the composer Ludwig van Beethoven was born in the rear building in December 1770.

name: Sunflower House
sub: Huge sunflowers bloom on a high-rise building in Wuppertal, providing more joy of life.
products: KEIM Klassik-MW, KEIM Soldalit-ME, KEIM Soldalit-grob, KEIM Brillantputz
story: Bright sunflowers on a blue background beautify the façade of a high-rise building in Wuppertal. In addition to a good mood, the building now also provides better air at the same time - thanks to a photocatalytic coating. A colourful sunflower stands for joie de vivre, cheerfulness and warmth.

name: Humboldt Forum
sub: How do you determine the historic colouring of a building?
products: KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Soldalit-Fixativ, KEIM Restauro-Lasur, KEIM Restauro-Fixativ, KEIM Optil
story: Used as the Humboldt Forum, the Stadtschloss Berlin houses modern exhibition rooms behind baroque facades that were created as a precise reconstruction. For the coloured sections, the planners relied on KEIM products. But how do you determine the historical colouring of a building whose last remains were blown up 70 years ago? With the reconstruction of the Berlin Palace, a piece of urban repair in the heart of Berlin is now complete.

name: Lagom Residential Complex
sub: The driving force for the architecture of a residential quarter was the shipping on the nearby lake.
products: KEIM Lignosil-Color, KEIM AquaROYAL-EPS, KEIM AquaROYAL-MW
colours: Farbton MFH = 9590, Farbton EFH/DH/RH = NCS S 7010-Y10R.
story: Either they turn grey unattractively or they are high-maintenance: there are many prejudices against wooden facades. The Lagom residential quarter on Lake Ammersee puts a stop to this. The complex relies on a colour-stable coating system for its outer skin of wooden slats, which is not only durable and easy to maintain, but can also be applied in advance. Residential quarter in Herrsching am Ammersee

name: Stadtsparkasse
sub: If you want to withdraw money, you can't get past the red facade of Munich's bank "Stadtsparkasse".
story: The square "Elisabethplatz" in Munich, where the bank "Stadtsparkasse" is also located, not only bears the prominent name of the legendary Empress Elisabeth "Sisi" of Austria, but is also a popular meeting place for the residents of Schwabing and all of Munich. If you want to withdraw money, you can't get past the red, thermally insulated facade of the Munich "Stadtsparkasse". And how could they not? Red has always been a registered colour trademark of the financial group "Sparkassen-Finanzgruppe".

name: Alnatura Campus
sub: Sustainability, transparency and a social corporate culture - this is what the new Alnatura headquarters stands for.
story: Where once army barracks and tank halls stood, there is now a unique "work, study, recreational and meeting place" with offices, a Waldorf kindergarten, a vegetarian organic restaurant and numerous leases and adventure gardens. The heart of the new headquarter of the German supermarket for organic food "Alnatura" is the Alnatura work environment - an open office landscape for up to 500 employees. This building is undoubtedly an ecological statement.

name: Panorama Swimming Pool Gruebi
sub: The panorama pool in Adelboden allows architecture, colour and nature to merge into one.
story: As a consistent example of the New Building style, the panorama pool in Adelboden is one of the most beautiful alpine open-air pools in Switzerland. The building, which has been classified as worthy of protection in the building inventory of the Canton of Bern since 2009, now shines again in its original colourful clarity. Again, one can clearly see the former spirit of optimism in the colourful open-air pool in the mountains.

name: Single Family Homes Munsky
sub: Hybrid construction of cool exposed concrete and warm solid wood plays a really supporting role here.
products: KEIM Granital, KEIM Lignosil-Verano, KEIM Concretal-Lasur, KEIM Stucasol, KEIM Brillantputz, KEIM Innostar, KEIM Innotop, KEIM Silan-100, KEIM Klassik-MW
colours: Verano 4870 applied several times, render and paint KEIM Exclusiv 9310
story: In the midst of housing estates from the 1930s, an architect built his own home and an apartment building. The result is two buildings that at first glance look like settlement houses, but on the inside they have a modern and reduced design with a combination of wood and concrete. A special project that was also characterised by sustainability. The small town of Kandel in the southern Palatinate is only a few kilometres from the French border.

name: Residential House
sub: Nestled in a magnificent landscape, this dream house reflects the attitude to life of its builders.
story: How do you make a dream house come true? For example, like the Scholz-Neuner family from Pegnitz in Upper Franconia: on a south-facing slope, with a dedicated architect and mineral products from KEIMFARBEN. The first stroke of luck was the building site. It is located on a sunny south-facing slope in the middle of a miners' settlement from the 1950s and offers an unobstructed view of the city all the way to the Schlossberg with its striking lookout tower. Then the architect came into play: "In the design process, the client's wishes were central to us from the very beginning," explains Volker Schwab.

name: Hotel Miramonte
sub: Colour treatment for a former spa hotel
story: The owners of the Miramonte gave the hotel a special mix of 60s charm and modern design. Restored wooden elements, newly upholstered armchairs, design classics and specially made pieces characterise the hotel, which is constantly evolving – with colour as an important design element. When Evelyn and Ike Ikrath, she a hotel manager and passionate hostess, he an architect, acquired the Miramonte in 2008, they deliberately wanted to preserve its brittle 1960s charm: The floors were refurbished, wooden fixtures restored, chairs reupholstered and reupholstered.

name: Atrium House in Weiden
sub: This atrium house interlocks simple and clear architecture with nature in an impressive way.
story: The declared goal of sustainable building is to achieve high building quality while conserving existing resources. This means the construction of buildings that are ecological, economical in the long term and durable in terms of construction technology and building culture, with a high quality of life and living. Whether it is a new building or an old one - sustainable construction and renovation requires energy-efficient planning and the selection of durable, pollutant-free and disposal-friendly materials.

name: Luitpoldbad
sub: Where kings once bathed, there is still a special flair in the air today.
products: KEIM Biosil, KEIM Soliprim, KEIM Granital, KEIM Universalputz, KEIM Innostar, KEIM Unikristalat
architect: Gerhard Grellmann / Rainer Kriebel / Christian Teichmann
builder: Free State of Bavaria - Zentrum Staatbäder Bayern, Bad Steben
story: There is still a special ambience that reigns within the walls of the old historic rooms of bath "Luitpoldbad" in the German spa town in the Bavarian region of Lower Franconia "Bad Kissingen". It is a unique place where once kings and emperors took their bath. Even after decades of vacancy and extensive repairs, many historical areas of the building complex have retained their special atmosphere. The measures went hand in hand with the Office for the Preservation of Monuments and protected the building ensemble from deterioration. Today, the bathhouse serves as a workplace for public authorities.

name: Villa Carlotta
sub: The white wooden villa called "Carlotta" fits perfectly into a 1920s housing estate.
story: The timber-cladded villa in Erfurt's Steinhalde bears the name Carlotta - composed of syllables from the first names of the owners' twin daughters, Carla and Charlotta - and is a reminiscence of the previous owners' summerhouse. Steinhalde is a steep path that can only be accessed as far as Villa Carlotta.

name: Residential Complex Gossau
sub: Through its colourfulness, the object radiates values: Reliability and durability.
story: Discreetly coloured, pragmatic and car-free, this is how the new housing estate "Im Eich" in the Swiss municipality of Gossau in the Zurich Oberland presents itself. Cows and goats graze in the surrounding meadows, and yet Zurich's main railway station can be reached from here in just over half an hour. The nine buildings with a total of 87 rented flats follow the topography of the gently inclined slope at different levels, creating a configuration based around semi-public courtyards that have been arranged in a variety of ways.

name: Schweighof
sub: What has been implemented here in terms of craftsmanship will likely be preserved in over a hundred years.
story: What remains is Mount Pilatus, Kriens' local mountain. Otherwise, in the still young canyons of houses and street deserts between the village centres of Horw and Kriens, hardly anything reminds one of the former idyll close to Lake Lucerne. If it weren't for the Schweighof development, part of a new Lucerne urban quarter being built on 76,000 square metres. The natural landscape of the past, which has disappeared forever, is emblazoned on the northern façades of recently completed apartment buildings. The unusual façade design brings to the fore a craft that links past, present and future.

name: French International School
sub: Pedagogical innovation and the learning of the future becomes a reality in Henning Larsen's school.
builder: French International School of Hong Kong
story: In Hong Kong's Tseung Kwan O district, sunlight hits the kaleidoscopic facade of the new French International School campus and penetrates the building through windows laid over a grid of 627 colourful tiles. This puts the 19,600-square-metre new school, designed by Henning Larsen Architects, at the forefront of educational innovation in Hong Kong.

name: Hunters Point Library
sub: The Hunters Point Library in New York differs from its high-rise surroundings through shape and colour.
story: The team around Steven Holl can also build smaller formats: On the banks of the East River in New York, the architect’s office realised a slender, cuboid building that can hold 50,000 books and captivates with its silvery facade. Compared to the neighbouring residential towers of Queens, the new public library at Hunters Point seems almost tiny. Nevertheless: The only seven-storey high and extremely narrow building has become a landmark. The strict basic shape of a high cuboid is opened up by cut outs and organically shaped, freely arranged glass areas.

name: Schmuttertal-gymnasium
sub: The grammar school in Diedorf proves: Sustainability and pedagogy can be closely linked.
architect: Arge Hermann Kaufmann + Partner ZT GmbH und Florian Nagler Architekten GmbH
story: Around 1,000 pupils at the Schmuttertal Gymnasium learn according to innovative concepts in a healthy, meaningful environment. In a construction period of only two years, a plus-energy timber school building was created as part of a research project of the German Federal Foundation for the Environment, which breaks new ground: open learning landscapes that can be used in a variety of ways enable individual learning and teaching. The architecture not only meets the latest pedagogical requirements, but also the strictest ecological building standards.

name: Royal Hobart Hospital
sub: Design that promotes health – for patients, relatives and staff
notes: Completed in 2020.
story: Completed in 2020, the Royal Hobart Hospital in Tasmania's capital city Hobart is part of a new generation of hospital projects in Australia. The concept by Melbourne-based architectural firm Lyons Architecture follows the principles of salutogenesis. The facade of the state-of-the-art urban community hospital is closely interwoven with its surroundings. The design is characterised by soothing surfaces, colours, artwork and views – everything to ensure the well-being of everyone involved, including patients, their families and staff.

name: Joan Kirner Women's & Children's Hospital
sub: Design for recovery
notes: Sixteen different Lasur colours.
story: The new multi-storey ward building of the Joan Kirner Women's and Children's Hospital in Melbourne heralds a new approach to the design of healthcare facilities with its colourful façade. The new health-oriented design is intended to provide orientation for patients and visitors, increase well-being and reduce stress. Colour, design and architecture can support the healing of patients - this has been known for a long time. In Australia, the Joan Kirner Women's and Children's Hospital in Melbourne and the Royal Hobart Hospital in Tasmania's capital Hobart are two special hospitals.

name: St Leonard's College
sub: Tradition meets innovation hub
story: St Leonard's College in Brighton, a suburb of Melbourne, was founded in 1910 and combines historic and modern architecture. The campus includes the striking Heritage Building and modern extensions, including the Innovation Hub, newly built in 2020, which offers interactive learning spaces. These refurbishments enhance the learning environment and encourage creative approaches to education. St Leonard's is known for its strong academic programmes and offers an inspiring atmosphere that harmoniously combines tradition and innovation.

name: Albany Ring Road bridge artworks
sub: Monumental bridge art by Glenn Hegedus for Main Roads WA
products: KEIM Concretal-Lasur, KEIM Faceal Oleo HD (anti-graffiti)
area: Thousands of m² of precast bridge abutments
notes: Main Roads WA changed its usual artwork policy to allow mineral paint here, and a second bridge project has already been approved with KEIM.
story: Along Albany Ring Road, artist Glenn Hegedus painted a series of bridge artworks drawn from the Great Southern’s rock formations, the coast of Princess Royal Harbour and stories shared on country with a Menang Noongar knowledge holder. Panels up to 9 metres tall were coloured with KEIM Concretal-Lasur, often through the night to beat the summer heat, giving the concrete a deep, flat, matte finish, then protected with KEIM Faceal Oleo HD anti-graffiti.

name: 201 Ellicott Street
sub: Affordable housing, fresh-food market and mobility hub with a mural by Josef Kristofoletti
story: A former surface car park on the edge of downtown Buffalo became 201 affordable apartments, a fresh-food market and the city’s first purpose-built mobility hub. Artist Josef Kristofoletti’s large mural is painted in KEIM Soldalit.
